title: Expression-tree realization and whole-system counit substitution
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Schemes $W$ are finite type over $k$, with small pro-etale sites and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived categories of strict semilinear systems $\mathscr S_W$ and the actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use simultaneous inverse images $P_v$, proper direct images $S_p$, quasi-compact open extensions $J_j$ and derived tensor, as in [def-sf-integral-system-operations]. Restrict inputs and intermediate systems to the domain of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]: derived-complete constructible integral inputs, normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, and common finite cohomological and Tor intervals. All conclusions below are restricted to expressions satisfying these intermediate-domain conditions.

Let $d_A:\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(K_i)$ and $d_c$ be the specified primitive and compactification comparisons of [lem-sf-integral-basic-realization]. Let $r_A:\mathcal R(A_{\rm int}(K_i))\to A(\mathcal R K_i)$ be the canonical whole-system coefficient comparisons, and assume their identities
$$r_A=e_{A(\mathcal R K_i)}\mathcal R(d_A^{-1}),$$
including the two-input version for tensor. Suppose $\mathcal R$ sends the complete input domain to the normalized system domain, $\mathcal L$ sends the normalized system domain to the complete input domain, and the actual $u_K$ and $e_M$ are invertible on these respective domains. For a normalized system $M$, and two systems $M,N$ for tensor, define
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal L M)\bigl(\mathcal L A(e_M)\bigr)^{-1},\qquad
 a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N)\bigr)^{-1}.$$
For a finite typed expression $V$ in variables, $P_v,S_p,J_j$ and tensor, write $M_V=V(\mathcal R K_1,\ldots,\mathcal R K_s)$ and $V_{\rm int}$ for its integral interpretation. The recursion
$$c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1},\quad
 c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)a_A(M_V),\quad
 c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)a_\otimes(M_V,M_T)$$
defines natural isomorphisms $c_V:\mathcal L M_V\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{\rm int}(K_i)$ for every such expression. It is a recursion on the finite tree, with each child smaller than its parent, including repeated variables.

Define whole-system coefficient maps recursively by $r_{K_i}=1$, $r_{AV}=A(r_V)r_A(V_{\rm int}(K_i))$, and
$$r_{V\otimes T}=(r_V\otimes^Lr_T)r_\otimes(V_{\rm int}(K_i),T_{\rm int}(K_i)).$$
They satisfy the specified equality of system maps
$$r_V=e_{M_V}\mathcal R(c_V^{-1})$$
with every quotient transition. The direct compactification comparison $d_c(K)$ agrees with the recursive $c_{S_p(J_j(K))}$, including the morphisms and all transitions specified in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The agreement uses the same open reduction map $r_j$ and the same proper-image tower, and concerns the prescribed comparisons. At variables the reduction equality is the triangle identity $e_{\mathcal RK}\mathcal R(u_K)=1$; at a unary or binary node it is the corresponding counit substitution identity. No compatibility with a structural generator is assumed or concluded here.

proof.text: Use the explicit natural coefficient recursion and its adjunction transpose from def-sf-integral-expression-recursion-data. The natural transformation is constructed recursively from the given primitive natural transformations, with both tensor slots retained. Its components are the given coefficientMap. The inverse hom-set equivalence proves the coefficient identity before any invertibility assumption.

By lem-sf-integral-expression-transpose-is-iso the restricted transpose has invertible components; componentwise invertibility gives an isomorphism of functors. Define c as its inverse. This is a real construction from the specified coefficient map, and the invertibility proof determines the inverse uniquely. The coefficient identity is the inverse-of-homEquiv identity, using c.inv equal to the transpose.

Apply lem-sf-integral-expression-canonical-equations pointwise to this c for the displayed tree equations, retaining the domain witnesses and their invertibility clauses. Pair these equations with the coefficient identity from the preceding step.

Apply lem-sf-integral-expression-canonical-support to this same c and the supplied direct comparison dc. It identifies the one-variable compactification branch with dc using its already supplied whole-system normalization. This completes the asserted existential and both clauses.
